Subject: Vector Gateway pilot: Searchlytics + Redwood

Hi Rishi / Vanessa,

Thanks for taking a beat to talk earlier this week — excited to follow up with a concrete pilot ask. Searchlytics has an enterprise customer (BrightLeaf Health) that needs a resilient hybrid retrieval layer: low-latency similarity search in-region, plus a cost-effective cold-store fallback for older vectors.

What we propose: a 6-week integration pilot where Searchlytics routes similarity queries through Redwood's Vector Gateway. Default path would be Pinecone for nearest-neighbor; on miss or TTL-expired state, Gateway should fall back to a pgvector/S3-backed cold lane run by Searchlytics. Pilot goals:

- Reduce 95th percentile retrieval latency to <120ms for common queries in us-west-2.
- Demonstrate transparent failover with <1% request loss during scheduled Pinecone maintenance windows.
- Collect cost deltas for tokenized recall + cold reads to build an econ model for BrightLeaf.

What we need from Redwood for kickoff:
1) A short network diagram (NAT, VPC peering or private link, IP allowlist)
2) Security checklist: supported KMS, audit log retention, data residency notes
3) A stub SLA for pilot test windows / support contact

Attaching a short proposal deck and a rough timeline. Happy to walk through this next Tue or Wed.

Attachments: [searchlytics-proposal.pdf (4 slides, pilot metrics & timeline)]

Best,
Emily Park
Head of Partnerships — Searchlytics Inc

Adding tech details so we can align on requirements before the call. Notes below — happy to expand during the sync.

1) Traffic profile
- Estimated QPS for pilot: 20 steady / 80 peak
- Typical query vector dims: 1536 (Open embeddings standard)
- Expected read/write mix: 90% reads, 10% writes (writes are batched hourly)

2) Integration pattern (recommended)
- Primary: Pinecone (region us-west-2)
- Fallback: pgvector index + S3 cold objects holding historical vectors and metadata
- Gateway should attempt Pinecone first; on 404/miss or >200ms tail, it should route to pgvector read path.

3) Data layout / snapshotting
- S3 path: s3://searchlytics-brightleaf/vectors/YYYY/MM/DD/segment-{n}.parquet
- Snapshot cadence: nightly full snapshot + hourly delta. Restore latency budget for cold hit <800ms (including S3 fetch).

4) Security / compliance
- We need mutual TLS for the service-to-service calls, and a signed IP allowlist for Pinecone control plane callbacks.
- Audit logs: retain 90 days for pilot; Redwood can ship logs to a customer-owned CloudWatch/Splunk endpoint.

5) Observability
- Redwood Console will emit per-request tags: partner=searchlytics, account=brightleaf, path=vector-gateway.
- We'll add a short trace hook to show fallback events so we can measure failover rate.

Action items (Ben):
- Prepare a minimal network diagram and a sample IAM policy for read-only S3 access (attached).
- Spike a tiny ngrok-less demo that simulates a Pinecone miss -> pgvector read.

-Ben
